decisions.quote:
We conducted four preregistered, high-powered replications of
Wilkins and Kaiser’s (2014) three original studies.
decisions.location: General Discussion, lines 325-326 (see also References, lines 490-492)
decisions.reason: Both the shipped record (listing the OnlineFirst year 2013, short title, and DOI 10.1177/0956797613508412) and blind target 0 (listing the 2014 print citation) identify the same target original article by Wilkins and Kaiser (2014) in Psychological Science (25, 439-446), whose three studies are directly re-tested by Studies 1, 2, 3a, and 3b.

decisions.quote:
It is clear that Wilkins and Kaiser’s (2014) original findings do
not replicate.
decisions.location: Conclusion, lines 397-398 (see also Abstract, lines 12-16; General Discussion, lines 328-336)
decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind code the outcome as 'failed'. Under Codebook Step 3 Rule 1, the authors' explicit overall verdict ('It is clear that Wilkins and Kaiser’s (2014) original findings do not replicate') governs over incidental agreements on the main effect of SLBs and the Study 2 manipulation check; none of the four focal SLB interaction effects were statistically significant in the predicted direction.

decisions.quote:
In three studies, Wilkins and Kaiser found that both chronic and experimental salience of racial progress in the United States
increased the perceptions of anti-White bias only among people high in status-legitimizing beliefs (SLBs). We conducted four
preregistered high-powered replications of this research.
decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind classify the record as 'replication'. The authors collected new data across four fresh MTurk participant samples (Studies 1, 2, 3a, and 3b) to re-test the published findings of Wilkins and Kaiser (2014).
